objectives.statement: Determine the equation of a straight line through two given points, using the gradient relationship and the standard form y = mx + c, and use it to find an unknown coordinate of a point known to lie on the line.
objectives.label: Equation of a straight line

evidence.quote: Straight lines
The standard form of the straight line equation is $y=mx+c$
The general formula for finding the equation of a straight line is $\dfrac{y-y_1}{x-x_1}=\dfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$
Find the equation of the straight line through $P\left(-1;-5\right)$ and $Q\left(5;4\right)$ .
Calculate the equation of the line $AB$ .

objectives.statement: Determine whether two lines are parallel, perpendicular or neither by comparing their gradients, and use that relationship to find an unknown coordinate or the equation of a line.
objectives.label: Parallel and perpendicular lines

evidence.quote: Parallel and perpendicular lines
the product of their gradients is equal to $-\text{1}$
Perpendicular lines have gradients that are the negative inverses of each other.

Line $AB$ is perpendicular to line $CD$ . Find $y$ given $A\left(2;-3\right)$ , $B\left(-2;6\right)$ , $C\left(4;3\right)$ and $D\left(7;y\right)$ .
Determine whether $AB$ and $CD$ are parallel, perpendicular or neither

objectives.statement: Determine whether points are collinear (lie on the same straight line), using the gradient method or the distance formula.
objectives.label: Points on a line

evidence.quote: Points on a line
There are two methods to prove that points lie on the same line: the gradient method and a method using the distance formula.
If two points lie on the same line then the two points are said to be collinear.
Prove that $A\left(-3;3\right)$ , $B\left(0;5\right)$ and $C\left(3;7\right)$ are on a straight line.
Find the sum of the two shorter distances

check.note: a0101 names 'a method using the distance formula' as one of the two ways to prove collinearity; a0103 spells out the step explicitly: to prove collinearity 'using the distance formula, we must calculate the distances between each pair of points' and compare sums; a0108 (WE9) then executes exactly that step, computing d_AB, d_BC, d_AC via the distance formula (leaving results as surds, e.g. sqrt(13), sqrt(52)) and using those distances to conclude collinearity. All three quotes are present verbatim in the anchored text, and together they show the dst objective (determine collinearity via distance method) using the src objective's method (distance formula, surd form) as a direct computational step, not just a shared topic word.
